text:
marie: heads up — noticed a steady memory increase on the kvcache with long-context workloads when continuous-batching is enabled. seems related to batch-merge keeping slot refs alive.

ashok: hmm. repro script?

marie: small repro attached. run ./tools/repro_kvcache_longctx.sh --seq 32k --qps 20 --contbatch on

kevin: got it. initial flamegraph shows hot path in kv_slot_acquire -> kv_fragment_pin -> batch_merge_bind

lia: can you paste the flamegraph snippet?

marie: ```
# top symbols (aggregated)
kv_slot_acquire  28%
kv_fragment_pin  18%
batch_merge_bind 15%
grpc_dispatch    10%
thread_pool_wait  6%
``` 

marie: also seeing lots of 'pin' counts in /proc/<pid>/fd. eviction isn't kicking in until fragmentation crosses threshold.

ashok: suspecting 'merge hysteresis' — when two batches merge we set slot affinity to merged head, but split doesn't clear affinity fast enough so tail requests keep the head pinned.

kevin: dev note: contbatch merge sets slot->owner = batch_id; split path only decrefs but doesn't reset owner until reclaim path runs. if reclaim is gated by eviction it's circular.

lia: interesting. so head-of-line blocking could be because head batch holds slot affinitiy and prevents eviction of stale fragments -> memory growth.

marie: repro logs show slow reclaim timers: ```
E 12:01:02 reclaim: fragment 0x7f3 failed try_reclaim (age 4s)
I 12:01:06 evict: skipped frag 0x7f3 pinned_by batch 12345
```

perf-bot: perf alert: kvcache resident set growth +18% over 30m on canary (contbatch=true)

ashok: quick fix idea — on batch_split path, immediately clear slot owner and bump a 'split-epoch' so any in-flight tail sees mismatched epoch and avoids re-pinning.

kevin: sounds reasonable. another approach: opportunistic async reclaim on split (spawn small background worker to try free fragments) — reduces reliance on eviction loop.

lia: what's downside? extra threads? contention?

ashok: worker is bounded and uses existing reclaim code with try_lock; cheap if few splits. biggest risk is extra latencies if reclaim runs inline; but we keep async.

marie: I'll prototype: batch_split -> clear_owner + enqueue_reclaim(batch_id). if reclaim can't grab lock, skip. will push PR to draft.

kevin: add metric kvcache.split_reclaim_attempts and split_reclaim_success

lia: test matrix: longctx seq 64k / contbatch on/off / reserved capacity 4g/8g

marie: running tests now, will post flames + heap profile

(2 hours later)

marie: update — prototype dropped growth from +18% -> +2% in 30m run. reclaim success ~86%.

kevin: nice. any regressions on latency?

marie: p50 unchanged, p99 +3ms under pathological merge storms. acceptable? :thinking_face:

lia: probably ok for now. let's tune backoff and worker batch size. also add unit test for split causing no pin.

ashok: open PR and label perf/urgent. we'll canary to dedicated and monitor metrics.

marie: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2921 (draft)

perf-bot: canary job scheduled: canary/kv-longctx-contbatch

kevin: thanks — nice catch. follow-up: audit other places we set slot->owner on transient ops.

marie: noted. closing thread once PR merges. :thumbsup:
